-`bbx` records what Claude Code does in your repository into an append-only, hash-chained log. When something breaks, it produces an incident report. It can tell you which lines were written by the agent, in which session, and from which prompt.
+`bbx` records what Claude Code does in your repository into an append-only, hash-chained log. Every prompt, tool call, file edit and command goes into `.blackbox/`. Later milestones turn that log into incident reports and line-level provenance ("which prompt wrote this line?").
 
-> Status: early development (Milestone 0). Nothing works yet beyond the skeleton.
+> Status: Milestone 1 of the v0.1 plan. Recording, `init` and `verify` work. `timeline`, `report`, `blame` and `investigate` come next.
 
+## Quick start
+
+```
+dotnet build -c Release
+cd your-project
+path/to/bbx init --local      # hooks point at this bbx binary (settings.local.json)
+# or, with bbx on PATH:
+bbx init                      # hooks go to .claude/settings.json, shared with the team
+```
+
+Then use Claude Code as usual. Check the log at any time:
+
+```
+bbx verify
+```
+
+## Commands
+
+| Command | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| `bbx init [--local] [--private]` | Creates `.blackbox/` and merges hooks into `.claude/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json` with `--local`). Existing settings and hooks are kept; a `.bbx-backup` copy is written first. Running it twice changes nothing. |
+| `bbx init --uninstall` | Removes bbx hooks from both settings files. Leaves `.blackbox/` alone. |
+| `bbx hook <event>` | Called by Claude Code. Reads the hook payload from stdin and appends one record. Always exits 0, never prints. |
+| `bbx verify` | Recomputes every session's hash chain. Exit code 1 if a record was edited, deleted or reordered. |
+
+## What it records
+
+One JSONL file per session in `.blackbox/sessions/`. Each line has `seq`, `ts`, `event` (raw hook name), `kind` (`PromptSubmitted`, `FileModified`, `TestCompleted`, ...), `actor`, `prompt_seq` (the prompt that led to it), event `data`, and `prev`/`hash` for the chain.
+
+- File edits: repo-relative path, diff (capped at 16 KB), added/removed line counts, normalized hashes of added lines, SHA-256 of the file before and after. Never the full file.
+- Commands: the command, exit code, the last 1 KB of output. Test and build commands are recognized (`dotnet test`, `npm test`, `pytest`, `cargo build`, ...).
+- Prompts: full text by default; `record_prompts` can be `hash` or `off`.
+
+## Privacy
+
+Redaction runs before anything touches the disk: API keys, GitHub tokens, JWTs, private keys, passwords in connection strings and `.env` lines, credentials in URLs, plus your home directory and user name. Files matching `ignore_paths` (`.env*`, `**/secrets/**`, `*.pem`, `*.pfx`, `appsettings.*.json` by default) are recorded as "changed" with no diff or hashes. Transcript and scratchpad paths from Claude Code are dropped.
+
+`.blackbox/` is committed by default so the team shares provenance. `bbx init --private` adds it to `.gitignore` instead. Redaction is pattern-based and can miss things; see [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md).
+
+## How it works
+
+```
+record[n].hash = SHA256( record[n].prev + "\n" + canonical_json(record[n] without hash) )
+record[n].prev = record[n-1].hash        (record[0].prev = "sha256:GENESIS")
+```
+
+The chain is **tamper-evident, not tamper-proof**. It catches edits, deletions and reordering inside a log. Someone with write access can still regenerate the whole chain from scratch. Anchoring the chain head in git commits is planned for v0.2.
+
+It also only sees what Claude Code passes to hooks. Commands you run in another terminal are not recorded.
+
+## Performance
+
+Each hook is a separate process, so start-up time matters. `bbx` is compiled with Native AOT. `scripts/bench-hook.ps1` measures it the way Claude Code calls it.

+| Build | Median per hook (Windows) |
+|---|---|
+| JIT (framework-dependent) | 128 ms |
+| Native AOT | measured in CI, see the `aot` job |

Milestone 1 bitti ve PR açıldı: [sayinbrahim/agent-blackbox#1](https://github.com/sayinbrahim/agent-blackbox/pull/1). CI şu an çalışıyor; AOT hızı da oradan ölçülecek, sonucu henüz görmedim.

## Ne çalışıyor

- **`bbx hook <event>`:** Claude Code'un yedi event'ini zincirli JSONL dosyalarına yazıyor: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd. Her koşulda exit 0 ile çıkıyor, stdout'a da stderr'e de hiçbir şey yazmıyor. Hata olursa `errors.log`'a yazıyor; bir kaydın üst süresi 2 saniye.
- **`bbx init`:** mevcut ayarları ve hook'ları koruyarak birleştiriyor ve önce yedek alıyor. İki kez çalıştırınca hiçbir şey değişmiyor. `--local`, `--private` ve `--uninstall` bayrakları var.
- **`bbx verify`:** kaydın düzenlendiğini, silindiğini veya sırasının bozulduğunu yakalıyor. Örnek çıktı: "tampered at seq 2 (prev hash mismatch)". Zincir kırıksa exit 1 ile çıkıyor.
- **Redaction:** secret'lar diske yazılmadan önce maskeleniyor. Buna ek olarak ev dizinin ve kullanıcı adın da maskeleniyor. Bunu, `ls` çıktısında adın göründüğünü fark edince ekledim.
- **Testler:** 133 test geçiyor (Core'da 117, CLI'da 16). Core'un satır kapsamı %95,3. AOT/trim uyarısı sıfır.

## Gerçek veriyle neler öğrendim

Sana sormadan geçici bir hook kurup bu oturumun gerçek payload'larını yakaladım; hook'lar oturumu yeniden başlatmadan devreye girdi. Bulgular:
- `transcript_path` alanı senin kullanıcı adını içeriyor. Bu alanı kayda almıyorum.
- Hata veren komutlar sadece `PostToolUseFailure` üzerinden geliyor ve hata metni `"Exit code N"` biçiminde.
- Edit sonucunda `originalFile` ve `structuredPatch` alanları var. Diff, before/after hash'leri ve satır hash'leri doğrudan bunlardan çıkıyor.

Bu payload'lar temizlenip `fixtures/` altına kondu.

 `bbx` records what Claude Code does in your repository into an append-only, hash-chained log. Every prompt, tool call, file edit and command goes into `.blackbox/`. Later milestones turn that log into incident reports and line-level provenance ("which prompt wrote this line?").

 ## Quick start

@@ -32,7 +32,31 @@
 | `bbx init --uninstall` | Removes bbx hooks from both settings files. Leaves `.blackbox/` alone. |
 | `bbx hook <event>` | Called by Claude Code. Reads the hook payload from stdin and appends one record. Always exits 0, never prints. |
 | `bbx verify` | Recomputes every session's hash chain. Exit code 1 if a record was edited, deleted or reordered. |
+| `bbx sessions` | Lists sessions: start, duration, prompts, tool calls, files, chain status, verification state. |
+| `bbx timeline [session]` | Prompts and the actions they led to, with failures and the verification state. Honors `NO_COLOR`. |
+| `bbx blame <file>[:line]` | Which lines the agent wrote, in which session and from which prompt; percentage for the whole file. |
+| `bbx report [session] [--format html\|md] [-o file]` | Single-file HTML incident report (no scripts, works offline), or Markdown for a PR description. |
+| `bbx investigate --commit <sha>` | Which recorded sessions produced a commit's changes (`exact`, `likely`, `none`), with prompts and build/test evidence at commit time. |
 
+`session` is an id prefix; it defaults to the latest session.
+
+## Verification freshness
+
+`bbx` recognizes test and build commands that the agent runs and tracks when source files change relative to them:
+
+| State | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `VERIFIED` | Tests passed after the last source change. That says the tests passed, not that the code is correct. |
+| `STALE` | Source changed after the last passing test run. |
+| `FAILED` | The last test run failed. |
+| `UNVERIFIED` | No test run recorded. |
+
+Changes to `*.md` and `docs/**` don't count as source changes (configurable under `freshness.exclude`). Test counts are parsed from `dotnet test` output; for other tools only the exit code is used, and counts are never guessed.
+
+## Provenance limits
+
+`bbx blame` matches whitespace-normalized line hashes from recorded agent edits of the same file. A line the agent wrote and nobody touched is found even if it moved within the file. A line that was changed afterwards counts as human. Lines in files the agent never edited while recording count as human or unrecorded. Blank lines and lines with only punctuation are not counted.
+
 ## What it records
 
 One JSONL file per session in `.blackbox/sessions/`. Each line has `seq`, `ts`, `event` (raw hook name), `kind` (`PromptSubmitted`, `FileModified`, `TestCompleted`, ...), `actor`, `prompt_seq` (the prompt that led to it), event `data`, and `prev`/`hash` for the chain.

+name: release
+
+# A v* tag builds Native AOT binaries and NuGet tool packages on each OS, checks that the tool installs and records,
+# then publishes to nuget.org (trusted publishing, no stored API key) and creates the GitHub Release.
+# Pull requests that touch packaging run the same jobs as a dry run (nothing is published).
+on:
+  push:
+    tags: ['v*']
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - .github/workflows/release.yml
+      - src/**/*.csproj
+      - Directory.Build.props
+      - scripts/release-notes.sh
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
+
+jobs:
+  version:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
+    steps:
+      - id: v
+        run: |
+          if [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
+            echo "version=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            echo "version=0.0.0-ci.${{ github.run_number }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          fi
+
+  native:
+    needs: version
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: true
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - { rid: win-x64, os: windows-latest }
+          - { rid: linux-x64, os: ubuntu-latest }
+          - { rid: osx-arm64, os: macos-latest }
+          - { rid: osx-x64, os: macos-latest }   # AOT cross-compiles across architectures, not across OSes
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
+    env:
+      VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
+        with:
+          dotnet-version: 10.0.x
+      - name: Publish native binary
+        run: dotnet publish src/Blackbox.Cli -c Release -r ${{ matrix.rid }} -p:Version=${{ env.VERSION }} -o out/${{ matrix.rid }}
+      - name: Pack RID-specific tool package
+        run: dotnet pack src/Blackbox.Cli -c Release -r ${{ matrix.rid }} -p:Version=${{ env.VERSION }} -o nupkg
+      - name: Archive binary
+        shell: pwsh
+        run: |
+          $rid = '${{ matrix.rid }}'
+          $name = "bbx-$env:VERSION-$rid"
+          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force stage, dist | Out-Null
+          $exe = if ($rid -like 'win-*') { 'bbx.exe' } else { 'bbx' }
+          Copy-Item "out/$rid/$exe", LICENSE, README.md stage/
+          if ($rid -like 'win-*') {
+            Compress-Archive -Path stage/* -DestinationPath "dist/$name.zip"
+          } else {
+            tar -czf "dist/$name.tar.gz" -C stage .
+          }
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: native-${{ matrix.rid }}
+          path: |
+            dist/*
+            nupkg/*.nupkg
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  pointer:
+    needs: version
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
+        with:
+          dotnet-version: 10.0.x
+      - name: Pack top-level (pointer) package
+        run: dotnet pack src/Blackbox.Cli -c Release -p:Version=${{ env.VERSION }} -o nupkg
+      - name: Pack framework-dependent fallback (any RID)
+        run: dotnet pack src/Blackbox.Cli -c Release -r any -p:PublishAot=false -p:Version=${{ env.VERSION }} -o nupkg
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: pointer
+          path: nupkg/*.nupkg
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  verify:
+    needs: [version, native, pointer]
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
+        with:
+          dotnet-version: 10.0.x
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          path: artifacts
+          merge-multiple: true
+      - name: List artifacts
+        run: ls -la artifacts
+      - name: Install the tool from the built packages and record one event
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          dotnet tool install AgentBlackbox --version "$VERSION" --tool-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/tool" --add-source "$PWD/artifacts"
+          bbx="$RUNNER_TEMP/tool/bbx"
+          "$bbx" --version
+          project="$RUNNER_TEMP/project"; mkdir -p "$project"; cd "$project"
+          "$bbx" init --local
+          CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$project" "$bbx" hook PostToolUse < "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures/hook-events/PostToolUse.bash-test.json"
+          "$bbx" verify
+          "$bbx" report --format md | head -20

+# Releasing
+
+Releases are cut by pushing a `v*` tag. `.github/workflows/release.yml` then:
+
+1. Builds Native AOT binaries on the matching OS for `win-x64`, `linux-x64`, `osx-arm64` and `osx-x64`.
+2. Packs one RID-specific tool package per platform (`AgentBlackbox.<rid>.<version>.nupkg`), a framework-dependent fallback (`AgentBlackbox.any.<version>.nupkg`) and the top-level package (`AgentBlackbox.<version>.nupkg`).
+3. Installs the tool from those packages on Linux, records a hook event and runs `bbx verify` (smoke test).
+4. Pushes the RID packages first and the top-level package last (installs fail if the top-level package arrives first), using nuget.org trusted publishing.
+5. Creates the GitHub Release with the binaries and the `CHANGELOG.md` section for that version.
+
+Pull requests that change packaging run steps 1–3 as a dry run with version `0.0.0-ci.<run>`.
+
+## One-time setup on nuget.org (trusted publishing)
+
+No API key is stored anywhere. GitHub Actions exchanges an OIDC token for a one-hour key.
+
+1. Sign in to nuget.org, click your user name, then **Trusted Publishing**.
+2. Add a policy:
+   - Repository Owner: `sayinbrahim`
+   - Repository: `agent-blackbox`
+   - Workflow File: `release.yml` (file name only)
+   - Environment: `release`
+3. In the GitHub repository: **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**, name `NUGET_USER`, value: your nuget.org profile name (not your email).
+4. In **Settings → Environments**, create an environment named `release`. Optionally add yourself as a required reviewer, so every publish waits for a click.
+
+Packages published to nuget.org can be unlisted but never deleted. Treat every tag as irreversible.
+
+## Cutting a release
+
+1. Move the `[Unreleased]` entries in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` section.
+2. Commit, merge to `main`.
+3. `git tag vx.y.z && git push origin vx.y.z`
